title: Seema Mitra award for BSF, SSB, cops from 2027; Rajnath pays tribute to war heroes at Sherathang
where: Nation, page 6 (Press Trust of India, Hingalganj and Gangtok)
syllabus: GS3 › Security challenges and their management in border areas · GS3 › Various security forces and their mandate · GS4 › Public service values (dedication, sacrifice)
summary: West Bengal will institute a 'Seema Mitra' award from 2027 for BSF, SSB and state police guarding borders, and promised more frontier police stations; Defence Minister Rajnath Singh paid tribute to war heroes near Nathu La.
ideas: Centre–state cooperation at the border: West Bengal shares over 2,200 km with Bangladesh; the state will facilitate more police stations in frontier areas with infrastructure, logistics and manpower.
GS3 · Border management
Border management needs state police and central forces working as one, as West Bengal's frontier police stations aim to do.
Morale and recognition: an award for exceptional contributions by BSF, SSB and state police acknowledges hard frontier duty.
GS3 · Security forces / GS4 · Motivation
Recognition like the Seema Mitra award sustains morale in forces guarding remote borders.
Sacrifice remembered: at the Sherathang war memorial on the India–China border, the Defence Minister said 'every generation of Indians will remember your sacrifice'.
GS4 · Public service values
War memorials keep alive the values of duty and sacrifice that public service rests on.
keywords: Integrated border management
Coordinated work of central forces, state police and civil agencies at borders
GS3 · Border management
Integrated border management joins central forces and state police in one system.
examples: BSF and SSB
BSF guards the India–Bangladesh border; SSB the borders with Nepal and Bhutan
GS3 · Security forces and their mandate
BSF and SSB show India's border-specific force design: one force, one frontier.
pyqs: China and Pakistan borders; BADP and BIM.

trend.t: Border questions moved from strategy (2016) and crimes across borders (2020) to specific programmes such as BADP and border infrastructure (2024, 2026).
trend.watch: Border infrastructure and development programmes were asked in 2024 and 2026, so Centre–state cooperation and force welfare are useful supporting points.
focus: Morale and welfare of border forces

potential: Discuss the role of state governments in managing India's international land borders. (10 marks)

title: Navy rescues hijacked vessel with Iran crew, IAF lends helping hand
where: Front page, continued on page 2 (Amrita Nayak Dutta)
syllabus: GS3 › Security challenges and their management in border areas (maritime security); Various security forces and their mandate · GS2 › India's bilateral relations (Iran); Effect of policies of other countries on India's interests (West Asia) · GS4 › Ethical issues in international relations
summary: The Indian Navy, backed by an IAF C-17 airdrop of Marine Commandos, freed the fishing vessel Azini and its 20 Iranian crew, hijacked by pirates off Somalia last month, in an operation of over 48 hours.
ideas: Piracy as a regional threat: the Navy saw the hijacked vessel as a likely 'mother ship' for launching pirate attacks on merchant shipping, so freeing it protects the sea lanes as well as the crew.
GS3 · Maritime security
Hijacked fishing vessels used as pirate mother ships make piracy a threat to the whole sea lane, not to one crew.
Jointness in action: a mission-deployed warship, a maritime reconnaissance aircraft and Marine Commandos airdropped by an IAF C-17 worked together.
GS3 · Security forces and their mandate
The Azini rescue shows inter-service jointness turning surveillance into swift action at sea.
Restraint as strategy: after persistent surveillance, the Navy used 'calibrated non-kinetic measures' to contain the vessel before its tactical intervention, and all 20 crew were released.
GS3 · Maritime security / GS4 · Proportionality
Calibrated, non-kinetic force secured the hostages' release without escalation: security achieved with restraint.
First responder and preferred security partner: the Navy framed the operation as proof of India's role in the Indian Ocean Region, regardless of the crew's nationality.
GS2 · India and the IOR / GS3 · Security
Rescuing foreign crews builds India's credibility as the Indian Ocean's first responder and preferred security partner.
Diplomacy through rescue: Iran's Embassy praised India's HADR commitment and called the rescue a testament to Iran–India friendship and cooperation.
GS2 · India–Iran relations
Maritime help to Iranian sailors turns hard naval capability into soft-power goodwill with Iran.
keywords: Mother ship
A captured vessel used by pirates as a floating base to attack ships far from shore
GS3 · Maritime security
Captured mother ships let pirates strike far out at sea, so freeing them is preventive security.
Non-kinetic measures
Using surveillance, blocking and pressure instead of firepower
GS3 · Security / GS4 · Ethics of force
Non-kinetic containment let the Navy secure the crew while keeping force to the minimum.
Preferred security partner
A country others in a region turn to first for maritime help
GS2 · IR / GS3 · Security
Every rescue at sea strengthens India's claim to be the Indian Ocean's preferred security partner.
Net security provider
A state whose capabilities provide security for the wider region, not only itself
GS2 · IR / GS3 · Security
Anti-piracy operations for other nations' crews show India acting as a net security provider.
HADR
Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief
GS2 · IR / GS3 · Disaster management
HADR operations let India's armed forces win friends without firing a shot.
examples: Rescue of the Iranian crew of the Azini
Navy and IAF free 20 Iranian fishermen from pirates
GS4
GS3 · Maritime security · GS2 · India–Iran · GS4 · Compassion beyond borders
India's rescue of 20 Iranian fishermen shows that compassion and duty at sea do not depend on the victim's nationality.
Navy–IAF airdrop of Marine Commandos
C-17 precision airdrop to a vessel far at sea
GS3 · Security forces · jointness
The C-17 airdrop of Marine Commandos is a ready example of jointness among the armed forces.
Calibrated force against pirates
Surveillance and non-kinetic containment before intervention
GS4
GS3 · Security · GS4 · Means and ends · Essay
Containing pirates without escalation shows that the most effective use of power is often the most restrained.
pyqs: Why maritime security is vital for India's sea trade; challenges and way forward.
Maritime security challenges and India's organisational, technical and procedural initiatives.
IPMDA as a bridge between SAGAR and the Quad's Indo-Pacific strategy.
Role of the IMO in the marine environment and maritime safety and security.
IMO's shift of the piracy high-risk area in the Arabian Sea and India's concerns.

trend.t: Maritime questions began with a narrow piracy-zone issue (2014), widened to India's overall maritime security architecture (2022) and the link between security and sea trade (2025). In 2023 and 2026 the frame moved to institutions and partnerships: the IMO, then IPMDA, SAGAR and the Quad.
trend.watch: Maritime security has been asked in 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026, so it is a must-study area. Questions now ask how India secures the seas through partnerships, not only its own navy.
focus: Threats at sea: piracy, attacks on shipping, chokepoints
India's institutions and initiatives for maritime security
SAGAR and India as a first responder in the IOR

potential: "The Indian Navy's role in the Indian Ocean Region is shifting from guarding India's coasts to securing the region's sea lanes." Discuss. (15 marks)
Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) has become a tool of India's maritime diplomacy. Examine with examples. (10 marks)
What challenges does the resurgence of piracy and attacks on merchant shipping pose to India's sea trade? Suggest measures. (10 marks)

practice.q: "The Indian Navy's role in the Indian Ocean Region is shifting from guarding India's coasts to securing the region's sea lanes." Discuss.

answer.t: In November 2026 the Indian Navy freed the Iranian fishing vessel Azini and its 20 crew from pirates, calling itself the 'first responder and preferred security partner' in the IOR.

pts.t: The Navy now acts against pirates far from India's coast because piracy threatens the sea lanes that carry India's trade.
pts.ex: Freeing the Azini, which could have been used as a pirate mother ship (2026).

pts.k: Protecting the shipping of all nations
pts.t: Rescues are carried out irrespective of the flag or the crew's nationality, building trust across the region.
pts.ex: 20 Iranian crew rescued; Iran's Embassy thanked India.

pts.t: Warships are kept on station in key areas round the year, so the Navy can respond quickly to incidents.
pts.ex: A mission-deployed warship intervened in the Azini rescue.

pts.t: Joint operations with the IAF extend the Navy's reach far out to sea.
pts.ex: Marine Commandos airdropped by an IAF C-17.

pts.t: Surveillance and information sharing let the Navy track threats across the region.
pts.ex: Information Fusion Centre – IOR at Gurugram; IPMDA with the Quad.

pts.t: Relief missions make India the first responder in crises across the IOR.
pts.ex: Operation Samudra Setu (2020) brought Indians home by sea during Covid.

pts.t: Attacks on merchant shipping in West Asia show how exposed India's trade and seafarers remain.
pts.ex: Indian-flagged sailing vessels attacked off Oman during the West Asia war (IE, 4 Nov 2026).

pts.t: The Navy's ships and aircraft are stretched across a huge ocean.
China's growing presence, including its base at Djibouti, competes for influence.
Fishing boats and sailing cargo vessels are hard to track and protect.
Sharing intelligence and responsibility with littoral states and partners is still uneven.
Prosecuting captured pirates across jurisdictions remains difficult, though India enacted the Maritime Anti-Piracy Act in 2022.
More ships, maritime patrol aircraft and unmanned systems for persistent watch.
Strengthen IFC-IOR and IPMDA links with littoral states.
Train and equip smaller IOR navies and coast guards under SAGAR.
Advisories, tracking and insurance support for small Indian vessels in risky waters.
Apply the Maritime Anti-Piracy Act and work through the IMO for common rules.
Continue non-kinetic, proportionate methods that resolve crises without escalation.

answer.t: From the Azini rescue to HADR missions, India's Navy is becoming the IOR's first responder; capacity and partnerships will decide how far that role can grow.

title: Flagship fest ahead, why Nagaland wants permit regime scrapped
syllabus: GS3 › Security challenges and their management in border areas; Linkages of development and security · GS2 › Federalism and Centre–state relations; Issues relating to the Northeast · GS1 › Tribal culture · GS4 › Citizen-friendly administration
summary: Nagaland has urged the Centre to completely withdraw the Protected Area Permit for foreigners, reimposed in December 2024 for security reasons, saying it hurts tourism ahead of the Hornbill Festival.
ideas: Two permits, two purposes: the PAP (Foreigners (Protected Areas) Order, 1958) controls foreigners' entry to border states, while the colonial-era ILP regulates Indian citizens to protect indigenous hill cultures.
GS3 · Border management / GS1 · Tribal culture
India's permit regimes serve two aims: security at the border (PAP) and protection of tribal cultures (ILP).
Security versus development: relaxed in 2011 and reimposed in December 2024 for security reasons, the PAP now clashes with the state's push for tourism and investment.
GS3 · Linkages of security and development
In peaceful border states, rigid security rules can choke the development that itself secures the region.
A rule from another era: the CM argues that a regulation designed for a different security environment should not hold back a peaceful state's aspirations.
GS2 · Governance / Policy review
Rules must be reviewed as conditions change; regulations that outlive their purpose become obstacles.
Process matters as much as policy: bureaucracy, a convoluted application process and last-minute relaxations deter foreign tourists who plan months ahead.
GS2 · Governance / GS4 · Citizen-friendly administration
Predictable, simple procedures matter as much as the rule itself for tourism and trust.
Federal voice: the state wants a central rule changed and has taken it to the Union Home Minister, but awaits a decision.
GS2 · Federalism
Nagaland's appeal on the PAP shows states seeking a voice in central rules that shape their development.
keywords: Protected Area Permit (PAP)
Central permit for foreigners to visit designated border areas
GS3 · Border management
The PAP balances border security against openness to foreign visitors.
Inner Line Permit (ILP)
Permit for Indian citizens to enter certain northeastern states
GS1 · Tribal protection / GS2
The ILP protects indigenous cultures from demographic and economic pressures.
Security–development nexus
The idea that development and security reinforce each other
GS3 · Internal security
In the Northeast, tourism-led development can strengthen peace as much as security controls.
Regulatory sunset
Reviewing or ending a rule once its purpose has passed
GS2 · Governance
A sunset review would test whether the PAP still serves security in peaceful states.
Cultural tourism
Tourism built on a region's living culture and festivals
GS1 · Culture / GS3 · Economy
Festivals like Hornbill turn culture into livelihoods and soft power.
examples: Hornbill Festival, Kohima
Flagship festival drawing visitors from across the world
GS1 · Culture · GS3 · Tourism · Act East
The Hornbill Festival is an example of the Northeast's cultural soft power and tourism potential.
PAP relaxed in 2011, reimposed in 2024
Security rule swinging with the security assessment
GS3 · Border management · GS2 · Federalism
The PAP's relaxation and reimposition show security policy shifting with threat perceptions.
Last-minute relaxations
Relaxation announced only around the festival gives tourists no certainty
GS4
GS2 · Governance · GS4 · Citizen-centric administration
A relaxation that comes too late to plan for is an example of form over substance in administration.
pyqs: Internal security challenges and peace accords in the North-Eastern States.
Security challenges in policing the border in North-East India beyond insurgency.
Border Area Development Programmes and civic action in Ladakh.
Challenges and strategies for effective border management.
Hill states reaching the limits of ecological carrying capacity due to tourism.

trend.t: Northeast questions moved from insurgency and border policing (2017, 2019) to peace accords (2025), while border questions shifted in 2026 to development programmes that win hearts and minds. The direction is from security alone to security through development.
trend.watch: The Northeast and border management are asked almost every year. Prepare the balance of security and development, peace processes and border-area development.
focus: Security and development in border areas
Northeast: peace processes and special arrangements
Permit regimes (PAP, ILP) and tribal protection
Tourism and the Act East policy

potential: "In India's border states, development is itself a security strategy." Discuss with reference to the Northeast. (15 marks)
Distinguish between the Inner Line Permit and the Protected Area Permit. Should the PAP be relaxed in peaceful northeastern states? (10 marks)
Examine the potential of cultural tourism in the economic development of the Northeast. (10 marks)

practice.q: "In India's border states, development is itself a security strategy." Discuss with reference to the Northeast.

answer.t: In November 2026 Nagaland asked the Centre to withdraw the Protected Area Permit, reimposed in 2024, arguing that a rule from another security era holds back a peaceful state's development.

pts.t: Livelihoods cut the pool of youth drawn to insurgency.
Visitors bring income and integrate the region with the world.
pts.ex: Hornbill Festival draws visitors from many countries.

pts.t: Roads, rail and air links bind border areas to the mainland.
Schools, health and services build trust in government.
Thriving villages deter infiltration better than empty borders.
Development sustains peace accords.
pts.ex: Peace accords in the Northeast in the past decade.

pts.t: Movement of insurgents, arms and drugs across international borders.
Instability in Myanmar affects the region.
Proximity to China calls for caution on foreign access.
The ILP shields indigenous identity from outside pressure.
Relax the PAP where conditions are peaceful, with safeguards.
Online, time-bound approvals that foreigners can plan for.
Involve states in decisions on central rules that shape their economies.
Technology at borders so that security does not depend on blanket restrictions.
Tourism, crafts and agro-processing for local youth.
Community-led tourism that respects indigenous ways of life.

answer.t: In the Northeast, a confident state secures its borders by opening its doors with care; balancing permits with prosperity is the surest path to lasting peace.

title: NSA Doval, Vietnamese ministers hold bilateral talks to boost security
syllabus: GS2 › Bilateral relations; Act East; Indo-Pacific · GS3 › Security cooperation
summary: Minor topic: NSA Ajit Doval held talks in Hanoi with Vietnam's defence, public security and foreign ministers to strengthen 'multifaceted' ties.
ideas: Security at the core of Act East: Doval met Vietnam's Defence Minister, Public Security Minister and Foreign Minister; both sides reviewed defence cooperation and agreed to strengthen it.
GS2 · India–Vietnam / Act East
Security and defence cooperation with Vietnam anchors India's Act East policy.
A partner in the Indo-Pacific: Vietnam, a key ASEAN state on the South China Sea, is central to India's maritime and regional strategy.
GS2 · Indo-Pacific
Close ties with Vietnam strengthen India's position in a contested South China Sea.
keywords: Act East Policy
India's strategic engagement with South-East Asia
GS2 · Foreign policy
Defence ties with Vietnam give substance to the Act East Policy.
examples: NSA Doval in Hanoi
Talks with Vietnam's defence, security and foreign ministers
GS2 · Act East, Indo-Pacific · GS3 · Security cooperation
Doval's Hanoi visit shows India deepening security partnerships in South-East Asia.
pyqs: Maritime security and freedom of navigation in the South China Sea.
Geopolitical significance of the South China Sea.

title: Why Delhi mustn't take its eyes off Pakistan-Maldives
where: The Ideas Page, page 9 (Aditya Gowdara Shivamurthy, ORF)
syllabus: GS2 › India and its neighbourhood; Bilateral, regional and global groupings · GS3 › Security challenges; Maritime security
summary: Maldives President Muizzu's state visit to Pakistan, with 20 MoUs including defence, shows the Maldives diversifying beyond India; the writer backs India's economic approach but says it must state its security red lines.
ideas: Diversification beyond India: Muizzu's visit produced 20 MoUs, from socio-economic sectors to cybersecurity, drugs and defence and maritime security, and a plan to scale up trade.
GS2 · India–Maldives
Small neighbours are hedging by diversifying partners, testing India's primacy in its neighbourhood.
A crowded defence space: the Maldives also has defence MoUs with China and Turkey, has bought armoured vehicles from the UAE and joined a Saudi-led maritime coalition.
GS2 · Neighbourhood / GS3 · Maritime security
Multiple defence partners for the Maldives crowd the Indian Ocean Region close to India's maritime boundaries.

Pakistan's wider play: since Operation Sindoor, Pakistan and China have held trilaterals with Bangladesh and Afghanistan; Pakistan has pushed SAARC revival, a South Asian bloc without India and a larger naval presence in the Bay of Bengal.
GS2 · Regional groupings
Pakistan is using new regional formats to dilute India's centrality in South Asia.

India's pragmatic economic diplomacy: T-bill extensions, debt restructuring, credit lines and currency swaps build leverage and goodwill without fuelling anti-India nationalism ahead of Maldivian elections.
GS2 · Neighbourhood First / Economic diplomacy
India's economic support builds leverage while avoiding the nationalist backlash that pressure would provoke.
Clear red lines on security: some MoUs (cybercrime, drugs) may even help India, but defence ties with Pakistan need clear communication of India's concerns.
GS2 · Foreign policy / GS3 · Security
India can accept the Maldives' diversification but must draw red lines on defence and security.
keywords: Strategic hedging
Small states balancing among several powers
GS2 · IR
The Maldives' outreach to Pakistan, China and Turkey is classic strategic hedging.
Neighbourhood First
India's policy priority for its immediate neighbours
GS2 · Foreign policy
Neighbourhood First relies on economic support to keep small neighbours close.
Economic statecraft
Using credit, aid and swaps to shape relations
GS2 · Economic diplomacy
India's currency swaps and credit lines to the Maldives are economic statecraft.
Red lines
Limits a country signals it will not accept
GS2 · Diplomacy / GS3 · Security
India must communicate red lines on Pakistan's defence role in the Maldives.
Crowded IOR
More extra-regional powers active in the Indian Ocean
GS2 · Indian Ocean
A crowded IOR raises India's maritime security challenges.
data: Maldives–Pakistan trade target for the next two years
Maldives–Pakistan agreements during the state visit, via IE
The Maldives and Pakistan aim to raise trade from $13 million to $200 million in two years.
examples: India's support to the Maldives
T-bill extensions, debt restructuring, credit lines and currency swaps
GS2 · Neighbourhood First, economic diplomacy, soft power
India's financial support to the Maldives shows economic statecraft winning goodwill without coercion.
Muizzu's defence MoUs with Pakistan, China, Turkey
A small state spreading its security partnerships
GS2 · Small-state hedging · GS3 · Maritime security

Pakistan's South Asian bloc idea
A proposed regional bloc without India
GS2 · Regional groupings (SAARC)

pyqs: Geopolitical and geostrategic importance of the Maldives for India.

trend.t: The Maldives was asked in 2013 for its political turmoil and in 2024 for its geostrategic importance to trade, energy and maritime security. Neighbourhood questions moved from domestic factors in foreign policy (2013) and SAARC (2016) to China's BRI turning South Asia into a theatre of competition (2026).
trend.watch: The Maldives has been asked twice, and island neighbours keep returning through maritime security. Prepare small-state hedging, India's economic diplomacy and extra-regional powers in the IOR.
focus: Pakistan and China in South Asian groupings

potential: "India's neighbourhood policy must balance economic generosity with clear security red lines." Discuss with reference to the Maldives. (10 marks)
Examine the implications of growing Maldives–Pakistan defence ties for India's maritime security. (10 marks)

practice.q: "India's neighbourhood policy must balance economic generosity with clear security red lines." Discuss with reference to the Maldives.
parts: Security red lines: why they matter

answer.t: Maldives President Muizzu's state visit to Pakistan produced 20 MoUs, including on defence and maritime security, even as India has extended credit lines and currency swaps to Malé.

pts.t: T-bill extensions, credit lines and swaps keep India the first responder.
Coercion would feed anti-India politics before elections.
Cooperation on cybercrime and drugs helps India too.
Defence MoUs with Pakistan, China and Turkey bring rivals closer.
A bloc without India and a larger naval presence.
The Maldives sits astride key sea lanes.

pts.k: Communicate red lines privately and clearly
pts.t: On defence presence and bases.
Health, connectivity and climate resilience.
Coast-guard and maritime-domain-awareness links.

answer.t: India should stay the Maldives' most generous partner while making clear that its security in the Indian Ocean is not negotiable.
